work_identified: Atisha Dipankara's Mala Divination (phreng mo) of Tara — 'jo bo rje dhi pam ka ras mdzad pa'i phreng mo'; the rosary divination prophesied by Tara to Atisha Dipankara (982-1054 CE), a short divination manual using mala beads attributed to Atisha and associated with the 21 Taras tradition

sources_consulted.found: British Library EAP confirms: this is 'jo bo rje dhi pam ka ras mdzad pa'i phreng mo' from Drametse Monastery Collection (Bhutan), EAP105 digitised manuscript
Brill publisher: Divining with Achi and Tara (Sobisch/Nielsen 2019) exists; description confirms Chapter 4 contains mala divination of Tara and its oral tradition contributed by Nielsen

Stanford catalog: Chapter 4 section 1 = 'Phreng Mo: A Popular Tibetan Way of Divining with a Mala'; section 2 = 'Tibetan Text and Translation of the Divination Manual of Tara' — Atisha not named in catalog subject headings but tradition attribution is widely attested
WorldCat record confirmed; Sobisch/Nielsen (2019) held in major academic libraries; Nielsen's Tara mala divination translation is the phreng mo section

Blog (2018): confirms Atisha's rosary divination on BDRC; author provides only rough unpublished partial translation of beginning; says Atisha divination 'transmitted by the Great 10th century Indian Buddhist master Atisha'
Tibeto-Logic (2013): 'brief rosary divination attributed to Atisha' from Kathmandu pecha mentioned as comparative; no full English translation
FPMT catalogue: no Tara Mo or phreng mo listed as formally published work; Lama Zopa version is draft-only, not a complete publication
Lotsawa House: 13 Atisha translations; none is a divination/phreng mo text
Interview confirms Sobisch (2019) focus on Achi Mo dice divination (Drikung); but Nielsen's separate Chapter 4 on mala/phreng mo is a distinct contribution covering the Tara tradition

reasoning: Chapter 4 of Sobisch/Nielsen (Brill 2019) explicitly presents 'Tibetan Text and Translation of the Divination Manual of Tara' within a chapter titled phreng mo/mala divination. Multiple independent sources attest this Tara mala tradition is attributed to Atisha. FPMT Tara Mo is draft-only. Lotsawa House has no phreng mo. Confidence medium: Brill chapter not directly accessed to confirm identical recension to Drametse.
